title: Exploring the effectiveness of a co-designed weight loss intervention for people recovering from breast cancer treatment
official: North of England Wellness through healthy fooD choices and ActivitY After Early Breast Cancer (NEWDAY-ABC) hybrid intervention-implementation trial
summary:
Background and study aims
Many people recovering from early breast cancer are living with being overweight, which can negatively impact overall health and quality of life. Excess weight also increases the risk of cancer recurrence, which may impact long-term survival. Supporting individuals to adopt healthy lifestyle behaviours that help them to manage their weight is therefore important. However, there is a lack of ongoing lifestyle support offered to individuals after the initial treatment. To address this, this programme worked with women with overweight after surgical treatment for breast cancer and healthcare professionals to co-design a lifestyle support programme. The programme aims to educate and empower people treated for early breast cancer to manage their weight by increasing their physical activity and improving their diet. The support programme has been tested in a previous small study, which found that women who received the support programme lost more weight than those receiving standard care. This study now aims to conduct a larger study with 375 patients recovering from early-stage breast cancer with a BMI over 25 to test how effective the support programme is, in comparison with standard care in supporting healthy weight loss.

Who can participate?
Patients aged 18 years or older diagnosed with early-stage, HER2-negative breast cancer and have completed all (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy, radiation and surgery at least 21 days prior to enrollment. Patients are required to be under the care of one of the four participating NHS Trusts.

What does the study involve?
Participants are randomly allocated to either the control or the intervention group. Participants allocated to the control group are asked to attend the initial assessment session and follow-up assessment sessions after 6, 12 and 18 months. They continue to receive usual care from their healthcare provider and, on completion of the 18-month assessment session, receive all the intervention materials that are given to participants in the intervention group.

Participants allocated to the intervention group attend an initial support session and attend support sessions over 12 months. These workshops offer healthy lifestyle (dietary and physical activity) education; support for the different ways to engage in physical activity; provide an opportunity for discussion and resolving personal challenges; and help through the weight loss journey. After the first 3 months in the support group, the lifestyle advisor contacts the participant at regular intervals, either by telephone or email (participant choice), to provide individual ongoing support.

All participants complete baseline, 6,12 and 18 months testing carried out by members of the research team who are blinded to group allocation. These sessions collect all outcome measures. A process evaluation is ongoing throughout the study. This evaluation includes interviewing lifestyle advisors leading the group sessions, interviewing participants at different timepoints and observing group sessions.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants allocated to the intervention group receive information and support regarding healthy eating and physical activity to achieve and maintain weight loss and improve their general level of fitness. This programme of support for lifestyle behaviour change has been specifically designed for breast cancer patients. The intervention will also inform the participants of the latest evidence-based guidance on dealing with possible side effects that they might be experiencing. By decreasing weight and becoming more physically active, current scientific evidence suggests that improvements in the quality of cancer survivorship experience, as well as decreasing risk of future health conditions, including breast cancer recurrence, diabetes and cardiovascular problems. Intervention groups involve a physical activity component, which could lead to some muscle soreness or risk of injury. These sessions will be progressive and will be taken by a qualified cancer-rehabilitation exercise instructor to ensure these risks are minimal. During group and individual coaching sessions with lifestyle advisors, participants may discuss topics relating to their cancer diagnosis that they find distressing. All participants will have the option to complete up to three Dual Energy X-ray (DXA) scans. All of these will be extra to those that they would receive if they did not take part. These scans provide clinical information. The X-ray procedures use ionising radiation to form images of the body. Ionising radiation can cause cell damage that may, after many years or decades, turn cancerous. The chance of this happening as a consequence of taking part in this study is extremely small.

Where is the study run from?
The study is sponsored by the University of Hull. The study visits will be held at the University of Hull, Sheffield Hallam University and the Christie NHS Foundation Trust. 

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
July 2026 to April 2029

Who is funding the study? 
Yorkshire Cancer Research, UK.

interventions.name: Participants will be identified by the breast care and oncology teams (including research nurses, breast care nurses, other healthcare professionals and consultants) in each of the associated NHS Trusts. This will be through outpatient breast cancer / oncology clinics and by the use of existing data

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Participants aged > = 18 within 36 months of the first histologic diagnosis of HER2-ve early breast cancer
2.	Stage 2 or Stage 3 early breast cancer
3.	BMI> 25 and/or waist circumference > 88cm.
4.	Completed all (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy, radiation and surgery at least 21 days prior to registration. 
5.	Concomitant hormonal therapy, bisphosphonates and CDK4/6 inhibitors are acceptable. 
6.	Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status 0 or 1 with no co-morbidities that preclude a lifestyle intervention.
7.	A patient at a participating NHS organisation
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Stage I and stage 4 breast cancer patients 
2.	HER2+ve diagnosis
3.	Participating in another weight loss, physical activity or dietary intervention clinical trial
4.	Currently on, planning on starting or within 6 weeks of the last dose of GLP-1 antagonists (Weight loss drug)
